title: Auto-Scaling, Load Balancing & FinOps Cost Governance
summary: Combine Application Load Balancers, Target Tracking Scaling, health probes, budgets, and Spot vs Reserved capacity planning.
learningObjectives: Design Application Load Balancers with graceful connection draining and target tracking scaling policies
Balance high availability against Cloud FinOps strategies (Right-sizing, Spot/Savings Plans, Billing Alarms)
prerequisiteConcepts: Understanding of stateless compute and AZs

sections.heading: 1. Elastic Scaling & Graceful Traffic Draining
sections.content:
Traffic spikes break fixed capacity servers while over-provisioning idle nodes burns budgets. Target Tracking Auto Scaling maintains target CPU/request utilization (e.g., scale out when average ALB requests-per-target exceed threshold, with cooldown periods preventing thrashing).

When load balancers terminate excess nodes during scale-in, connection draining (deregistration delay) holds existing in-flight HTTP requests safely while halting new routing immediately—preventing sudden 502 Bad Gateway disruptions.

codeExamples.code:
Client HTTPS -> [Application Load Balancer (TLS Termination)]
                  | Health Checks: GET /api/health (HTTP 200 OK)
                  +---> [Auto Scaling AZ-A Instances] (CPU Target 60%)
                  +---> [Auto Scaling AZ-B Instances] (Graceful Drain: 30s)
codeExamples.explanation: Load balancers isolate failed nodes dynamically and honor connection draining during Auto Scaling scale-in events.

keyPoints: Prefer Target Tracking scaling over brittle static cron schedules for organic user spikes.
Set Billing Alerts and Budget Thresholds on day one in every cloud account to catch runaway loops early.
commonMistakes: Scaling out slowly (10 minute startup) with tight aggressive scale-in cooldowns causing constant thrashing.

sections.heading: 2. FinOps Capacity Tiering & Budget Guardrails
sections.content: Production FinOps blends steady baseline commitments (Savings Plans / Reserved Instances for 24/7 core traffic), stateless burst Spot capacity for batch jobs, and automated budget alerts triggering Slack/PagerDuty notifications before costs escalate.

codeExamples.code:
# Target Tracking Auto-Scaling Specification
scalingPolicy:
  metricType: ALBRequestCountPerTarget
  targetValue: 500
  scaleOutCooldownSeconds: 60
  scaleInCooldownSeconds: 300
  minCapacity: 2   # Ensures minimum 1 healthy node per Availability Zone
  maxCapacity: 20
deregistrationDelaySeconds: 30
codeExamples.explanation: Asymmetric cooldowns scale out rapidly under sudden traffic surges while scaling down gently to avoid flapping.
codeExamples.expectedOutput: Balanced fast scale-out (60s) with conservative scale-in cooldown (300s) and zero-drop draining

keyPoints: Maintain `minCapacity >= 2` distributed across 2 AZs for high availability.
commonMistakes: Setting `minCapacity = 1` on customer-facing services, guaranteeing downtime during AZ maintenance or single crash.

exercises.title: Zero-Downtime Auto-Scaling & FinOps Plan
exercises.objective: Prevent 502 errors during rolling scale-in and optimize steady vs burst cloud compute spend.
exercises.description: An API drops HTTP requests during afternoon traffic scale-downs and spends 100% On-Demand pricing on steady 24/7 containers plus nightly fault-tolerant Spark ETL batch workers.
instructions: Configure deregistration delay and SIGTERM handling to cure afternoon 502 errors.
Recommend distinct capacity purchasing tiers for 24/7 web API vs interruptible nightly ETL batch jobs.
exercises.starterCode:
# Remediation & Cost Optimization Plan
- 502 Scale-in Fix: ...
- Steady 24/7 API Tier: ...
- Interruptible Batch ETL Tier: ...
hints: Savings Plans / Reserved cover steady predictable baselines cleanly; Spot slashes costs for fault-tolerant batch jobs.
exercises.submissionRequirements: Complete all checklist items, test assumptions, and document verification rationale.
evaluationCriteria: Addresses the root architectural/technical challenge accurately
Follows defensive industry standards and edge-case validation
exercises.solutionExplanation: Deregistration delay drains open sockets during scale-in; Savings Plans optimize 24/7 API cost while Spot powers interruptible ETL cheaply.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Why do auto-scaling policies typically use shorter scale-out cooldowns (e.g., 60s) and longer scale-in cooldowns (e.g., 300s)?

options.text: To respond quickly to rising load while preventing premature capacity teardown during bumpy traffic lulls
Because scaling in triggers expensive license checks
Load balancers forbid adding nodes faster than removing them
To force CPU to remain permanently at 100%

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Fast scale-out preserves latency; conservative scale-in prevents oscillation thrashing.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Which cloud purchasing strategy reduces compute cost dramatically for fault-tolerant stateless batch rendering?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Spot capacity offers ~70-90% discounts on reclaimable compute capacity.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What protects in-flight user requests from abrupt connection reset errors when an Auto Scaling group removes an instance?

options.text: Load balancer connection draining / deregistration delay paired with graceful SIGTERM handling

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Connection draining halts new traffic while allowing existing open responses to complete cleanly.

recap: You engineered multi-AZ Auto Scaling policies, graceful load-balanced draining, and cloud FinOps budget discipline.
